question: What will the first reported earnings per share after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Apple)

calls.reasoning: Consensus ~$1.98-1.99 (27 analysts, $1.93-2.06); Polymarket's contract references a $2.02 GAAP estimate. Guidance (rev +9-11%, GM 47-48% incl ~1pt tariff refunds, opex $19.1-19.4B, tax 16.5%, ~14.6B shares assumed) implies ~$1.95 midpoint, ~$2.02 at top end. Apple habitually lands at/above the top of guidance and beat by 7% last quarter ($2.02 vs $1.89, incl $0.11 tariff refund) and ~6% in Q1 FY26. Polymarket prices an 81-87% chance of beating $2.02 GAAP; that book is not an exact match for the resolution criteria and beat markets lean optimistic, so it is discounted — I put P(>2.02) near 72%. Main tail risk is a one-off tax/legal charge (e.g., the Q4 FY24 EU charge). The release is scheduled for Nov 2 after the close.

July guidance (revenue +9-11% YoY on $102.5B, gross margin 47-48% incl. ~1pt tariff refunds, opex $19.1-19.4B, tax ~16.5-18%, ~14.6B shares) implies ~$1.95-1.98 at the midpoints and ~$2.04 at the top. Apple has beaten by 4-8% recently and usually lands near the top of guidance, so the median is ~$2.05. Polymarket's 'beat $2.02' contract at ~81-87% is very thin (~$1.1k) and only lightly weighted. The low tail is memory and supply pressure; the escape below the range would need a one-off tax charge like FY24's EU charge, and would have to be larger than that one.
calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on the facts: consensus ~$1.98, guidance inputs, beat history, Q3 diluted shares of 14.715B, and the release not yet out. The one factual dispute is the Q4 tax rate: run 1 cites a 16.5% guide, run 2 found none, and run 3 used ~18% from Q3's actual. It cannot be settled without web access and is worth ~$0.03, so I carried it as extra spread. The rest is judgment: how big a beat to expect and how much weight to give the thin Polymarket book. I take a median of ~$2.05 (about a 3.5% beat, in line with recent history) and give the market little weight because of its ~$1.1k volume. I agree with runs 1 and 3 on the low-tail mechanism but put it at 0.5%, since leaving the range needs a charge of ~$15B. I keep no upper escape because EPS above $2.995 is implausible.
